text:
sarah.sales: Atlas Financial just escalated to execs. CISO is saying we can't start the POC unless we solve three things: 1) private network peering (they prefer Azure ExpressRoute but asked about VPC peering options), 2) SAML + SCIM SSO + BYO-KMS for keys, and 3) a pricing cap for the POC (they want cost predictability for the trial). Need an internal exec bridge — who can own the technical answers?

alex.eng: I can take peering. Quick question — do they need L3 routing (BGP) or just NAT egress? If they want ExpressRoute with private peering we need partner/network team input and a support ticket. :thinking_face:

priya.security: BYOK and SAML are doable but host choice matters. If they require BYOK + HSM-backed keys we should push Private deployment (VPC) or Dedicated with KMS integration. Hosted API doesn't support customer-managed HSM today. Also need to confirm log retention & SOC2 outputs for their compliance team.

jess.se: Pricing ask — they want a hard cap for the 4-week POC, plus a short SLA on tail latency (<200ms 95th). Sales asks for an exec-level discount if we commit to a 6-month reserved capacity after POC.

tom.prod: Quick product note: Dedicated capacity can give them BYOK via KMS and predictable throughput. We have a standard POC SKU for finance verticals that includes a 20% trial discount and up to X reserved units for 30 days. SLA on latency will depend on model and qps; need model + traffic profile to commit numbers.

alex.eng: For peering options: if they want ExpressRoute private peering we can route via our VNET peering to their circuit. If they prefer IPsec site-to-site we can stand up a VPN edge in their region as a stopgap. Both require IP allowlist changes and egress firewall rules.

sarah.sales: @alex.eng + @priya.security can you confirm a recommended path by EOD? I promised the AE an internal unblock call at 10:30am tomorrow with their CISO and CTO. I'll run the exec bridge.

priya.security: Action: I'll draft the BYOK/KMS options and list of docs they need (attestation, key rotation policy, encryption in transit details). ETA 5pm PT. Also attaching the questionnaire snippet they sent:

priya.security: ```
Q12: Do you support customer-managed keys (BYOK)? If yes, describe key lifecycle and proof of HSM backing.
Q18: Can you support dedicated network peering (ExpressRoute or equivalent)? Provide steps and expected lead time.
Q27: Do you log raw request payloads? Retention and redaction policy?
```

alex.eng: I'll map out the peering options and a rough timeline. Short summary: ExpressRoute = 3-4 weeks to validate + network partner, VPN = 1-3 days for proof-of-concept (no dedicated SLA). I'll post the network diagram and sample IP allowlist.

ops-bot: Deploy ticket created — #INC-4821 for peering setup. Assigned to network-oncall. ETA initial triage 2h.

tom.prod: Pricing: I can offer a temporary POC cap with usage guardrails — e.g., disable burst autoscale beyond baseline, and apply hard quota. Sales discount proposal: 25% off list for a 6-month commit. Need approval from revenue ops for exceptions.

jess.se: I'll coordinate revenue ops and get the pricing decision. If they sign a short MOU committing to post-POC evaluation, we can fast-track discount.

ryan.cto: Heads-up from exec: if Atlas is strategic (finance tier), we should prioritize. I'm available for the customer bridge if needed. Recommend we prepare a one-page exec brief for the call: risks, mitigation, ask (security signoff + network lead + pricing ok).

sarah.sales: Agreed. Plan for tomorrow: 1) alex — bring peering options + rough ETA, 2) priya — BYOK doc + questionnaire answers, 3) tom/jess — pricing cap proposal, 4) ops-bot/network — quick triage and any gating tickets. I'll schedule 10:30am bridge and send invites.

alex.eng: Noted. I'll put the sample IP allowlist here after lunch. :thumbsup:

priya.security: Also flagged legal for contract clause around key custody and audit access. They might ask for escrow language — pinging @legal separately.

sarah.sales: Perfect. If we get the docs and the network plan today we can avoid exec escalation tomorrow. Thanks team. :pray:

jess.se: minor note — if they insist on ExpressRoute and BYOK simultaneously we should recommend Dedicated (short trial) to keep rollback options simple. I'll include that in pricing doc.

alex.eng: IP allowlist stub: `10.10.100.0/24` (example), ports 443/tcp allowed, BGP ASN if ExpressRoute: `65010` — will refine.

sarah.sales: Last thing — their CTO asked for a one-line SLAP commitment for execs to read. Can someone draft a neutral line we can show them?

tom.prod: Draft SLAP line: "During the POC we will commit to a median latency target appropriate to the selected model and baseline throughput; dedicated capacity options are available for guaranteed 95th percentile latency targets with reserved commits." Feel free to tweak.

sarah.sales: Great — saving this. I'll send invites and the exec brief draft in ~90m. Closing thread but will update with bridge calendar link. :rocket:
